content.intro: This lesson covers Hardware Constraints and Resource Budgets. It sits in Module 25, Embedded Rust and no_std, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Hardware Constraints and Resource Budgets matters when you work with toolchain and compiler feedback. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Embedded Rust must fit the target’s processor, memory, timing, and hardware constraints. no_std removes the standard library, so available APIs and startup/linking responsibilities depend on the target.

content_blocks.title: A reliable way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: For Hardware Constraints and Resource Budgets, write down the inputs, the guarantee you expect, and the boundary where that guarantee stops. Work through a minimal example first; then deliberately test one edge case. Hardware-specific modules require a supported target and often a device or emulator. The sample code is concept-focused and will not exercise a physical peripheral by itself.
